_about: The baptistery. 2026-10-08 (Josh): the modern water from SPAROOM applied here too -- the bath's water (ZQcutter01/02 at y -38 over zxwater at y -57, x 44..81, z 81..216) rippled, shiny and lit from below, with caustics on the bath and the wall beside it. Same look as SPAROOM's final settings, scaled to a bath: one lamp under its middle, a finer web, less height, and about half the light on the walls (the green moss turned the full strength neon).
_round25: Room Review BAPTIST/1 (round 25, 2026-10-14, Josh): 'Similar to how you cut out the grid in the minehead room, I want these windows to be cut out ... transparent with 30% opacity of the current pale portion of the glass. Then, I want warm light to flood though the grid at an angle that comes in and descends toward the ground for all windows on this side.' The six windows painted on the east wall (x 80, leftwall + leftwall01, three each: y 152..224 at z -96, 3, 101, 198, 297, 396): their panes cut out (holes) and drawn back as glass at 30% of their own pale colour, warmed by the sun behind them; the bars stay solid. Two warm suns outside, one for each half of the room (the mirror wall at z 148 between them), 300 units out, coming in 50 degrees below level, shadowed -- so the window grids fall across the room -- one-sided, so they never light the wall's inner face, and GATED to the windows' band (the room has no ceiling: without it the sun came in over the walls too). A thin haze so the beams show in the air, inside the room only.

holes._note: the three windows' panes (glass 40..160 bright in the original art, the bars 0..21): cut where at least 36 bright inside each window, then drawn as glass at 30% of their own colour, tinted by the sun behind them
